I barely played the first Remnant, it just didn't click with me. Remnant 2 on the other hand had me hooked almost instantly.

The visuals and sound design are great. The game play feels good. The only con I can think of currently, and it's kind of a big con for me, is how their coop is set up.

There are no regional settings, or ping settings or any means of communication from inside the game with whomever you coop with (other than a weak ping system). The stability inside of coop feels very hit or miss. I'm located in CST USA, about 3/4 of the time I'm paired with someone who has Asian characters in their name... so here comes the bad latency. The majority of coop games either end up not connecting or losing connectivity while playing. 

As the host, if a random joins your campaign, they can interact and make quest decisions without your input... this is horrible. I end up placing my game on Friends Only mode, since this is the only mode that doesn't default to Public once you join another players game.

Once you lose connectivity or are kicked you have to start all over from the character select screen, then load back into the game. 

So most often the "game play loop" ends up being: choose character, begin game, load Ward 13 (home base), select join game, pick someone's instance (all you see is their name and in-game location) or click quick play, end up not connecting after about a minute, get kicked to you're character select screen, restart loop.

If you happen to get into a game with someone who knows what they're doing, you may be SOL. There are no in-game tools to friend or find that person again. You can try typing their Steam name into Steam's search, but if it's a common name or they don't recognize yours nothing will come from it.

My last 10 minutes in game: I logged in, went to Ward 13, joined someone's campaign using QP, didn't connect, sent to character select, loaded the game again, chose QP again, loaded into someone's game, they happened to be resting so they were able to load me in pretty fast (if you catch someone running around the map nowhere near a checkpoint you can be stuck waiting for a looong time), helped them kill a boss, lost connection, once the character select loaded I turned the game off.

Thumbs up for the game play and quality. Thumbs down for the crappy implementation of coop.

Amazingly fun. I really have enjoyed it. Game play is solid and there are tons of fun and satisfying secrets to find. Lots of character customization also along with some really fun and interesting worlds to explore! Finally, the co-op game play is some of the best I've experienced in recent years. All that said, there are a few caveats and complaints I have. 

Mostly there are a lot of "1 hit" kill mechanics on some of the bosses now that aren't very fun too deal with and make the idea of playing Hardcore very unappealing. Lastly, the lack of the original's Survival mode feels like it was a huge mistake. I'd also love to see more areas fleshed out or given the "adventure mode" treatment as well. I suppose the conclusion to the main story arc feels less satisfying and more of a set up for the inevitable DLC also but that is more of a minor complaint. Still, a ton of fun!

Remnant II is to 2023 as Elden Ring was to 2022 for me.  Sprawling levels, decent difficulty, great story/character design, fantastic puzzles.  All of the ingredients are there!

My favourite things:
- The way the sessions vary.  A friend and I agreed that we would do our first play through together.  Sometimes we come away feeling like we're playing an action game, other times an RPG, other times a puzzle game.  Depending on where you are in the game the feel differs markedly and it's awesome.
- The world variety.  Each of the worlds has a very distinctive feel, adding to the sense of variety.
- The puzzles.  They're ideal for a non-casual but also non-hardcore gamer.  They're obtuse and challenging, but accessible enough to figure out.  My playing partner and I were blown away by one puzzle in particular that actually required both players to act in concert and had another unexpected nuance.  Great attention to detail from the designers/developers.
- Unique bosses with well calibrated difficulty (i.e. hard enough to whup your *ss a few times but not so difficult that you're tempted to throw a controller).  You get that sense of accomplishment without getting overly frustrated.  Battling rolling electronic cubes in the labyrinth = gold. 
- Lot's of replayability.  So much potential for different builds, exploration, collection etc.

Minor complaints:
- Despite the crazy variety across the various worlds, the procedural generation of each one leads to some of the worlds feeling a bit "samey".  It's not a big deal in the grand scheme of things, but it did creep up from time to time.
- As you progress, and especially if you explore thoroughly, the difficulty level diminishes as you approach end game.  Granted, my playing partner and I have been excessively thorough in exploring every nook and cranny of every map, but we're borderline OP starting the final world.  That said, I'm glad that I didn't have a Commander Niall kind of experience with this game.

Overall this was a great purchase.  I usually just buy the base game and expand if it catches me.  I'm not sure why, but when I pulled the trigger on Remnant II I went for the ultimate edition mainly so I'd get the bundled DLC.  I'm really glad I did, because I'm very much looking forward to seeing what the devs have in store.  Definitely my favourite game of the year so far!
